content.comment_body: I need to monitor the open and close actions of an air piston. I currently have one microswitch installed. I want to be able to open and close the piston, have the microswitch indicate both states, and ideally have it signal a failure if the piston does not open within a specific time limit, such as 5 seconds. How can I achieve this?

With a single microswitch, you can only detect one condition: either when the piston is fully extended and remains extended, or when it's retracted and remains retracted. Avoid checking the position alone. Implement the microswitch together with a movement command and a 5-second delay. If the switch-on delay expires, generate a message to indicate that the piston hasn't moved from its end position.

My plan is to use one microswitch so that it turns off when the piston opens and turns back on when closed. If neither state is reached within a set time, display a FAIL message. Does that make sense?
Using just one microswitch doesn't provide complete monitoring. When the switch changes state, you only know the piston left one end position, but you cannot confirm if it reached the other position.
That's a good point — my initial idea was flawed. How could I set this up with two microswitches?
I've attached a circuit diagram that illustrates the basic concept.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are exploring reliable ways to detect both open and closed positions for an air piston using microswitches, as well as creating a system to identify failures when the piston doesn't transition within a set time. The conversation highlights that a single microswitch is not sufficient for complete monitoring, which has led to recommendations for using additional switches and logic to ensure accurate position detection.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a dependable method to track both open and closed piston positions and to receive error alerts when the piston fails to reach a position within a defined time.
